subject: maths
question:
A sphere of radius 14 cm is cut along three diametrical planes to form 6 equal parts. What would be the total surface area (in cm²) of all the new pieces so obtained?

(Take pi = frac {22}{7})
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Original sphere surface area = 4πr² = 4π(14²) = 2464

3 diametrical cuts ⇒ each gives 2 circles ⇒ total new circles = 6

Area of one circle = πr² = 616

New area = 6 × 616 = 3696

Total surface area = 2464 + 3696 = 6160

**∴ Answer = 6160 cm²**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius = 14 cm; π = 22/7

**Formula used:**

Surface area of sphere = 4πr²; Area of circle = πr²

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acceb116470e866d4e44ed8df7fee062558649b7c129a798e15a0de36e4fee2e.png] 

⇒ Original surface area = 4πr² = 4 × (22/7) × 14² = 2464

⇒ Each diametrical cut creates 2 circular faces

⇒ Total cuts = 3 ⇒ New circular faces = 6

⇒ Area of one circle = πr² = (22/7) × 14² = 616

⇒ Total new surface area = 6 × 616 = 3696

⇒ Total surface area = 2464 + 3696 = 6160

**∴ The correct answer is 6160 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sphere Surface Area

4πr²

Diametrical Plane

Cuts the sphere into equal halves

New Surfaces

Each cut introduces 2 circular faces

Key Idea

Total surface = original curved area + new flat areas
